combination_principles.rule: Add the keywords: a combination is read by adding up each card's core keyword into one sentence, then shaping that sentence to fit the question. Start with two cards and build up from there.
The whole layout gives the answer, not any single card. Read every card in the context of the others and the question before settling on an interpretation.

A Major Arcana card sets the scene for the whole reading, and the Minor Arcana cards relate back to it. When Majors make up half or more of a spread, the reading is more fixed and life-changing; with few or no Majors, it is more flexible and changeable.
Minor Arcana cards in a spread with a Major Arcana card are drawn into that Major's sphere of influence: the Major names the big theme and the Minors show how it plays out in everyday life.

Cards with the same number share a theme across suits and elements. A Three of Swords and a Three of Cups are the same theme on different levels, and the Major card of that number (for example, III The Empress over all the Threes) names the theme they share.
Parallel cards share a final digit and echo each other as base tone and octave, or foreground and background: for example, V The Hierophant and XV The Devil, or VII The Chariot and XVII The Star.

Adding the cards' numbers can unlock a card: the Quintessential card is the digit-sum of a whole layout, reduced to a Major Arcana card, and names the layout's underlying theme. Two cards can also be added to explain a third (for example, II + III = V).

Count the elements in a spread: Wands are fire (passion, action), Cups are water (feeling), Swords are air (thought), Pentacles are earth (resources, body). A dominant element colours the whole reading, and a missing element is information too — it names what the situation lacks.

Friendly elements strengthen each other: fire and air feed each other, and water and earth support each other. A spread heavy in one of these pairs reads as fast-moving and intense (fire-air) or slow, healing, and grounded (water-earth).

Opposing elements weaken each other: fire is put out by water and earth, and water and air cannot support each other. When opposing suits sit together, read both cards as muted, strained, or in conflict.

Air and earth dilute each other rather than strengthening or cancelling out: they can sit side by side, but they feel opposite — air light and quick, earth slow and dense — so neither card dominates the other.

A court card's rank adds its own element to its suit: Pages are earth, Knights are fire, Queens are water, Kings are air. A court card whose rank and suit share an element is doubled and intensified — for example, the Queen of Cups is double water, so her intuition runs especially strong.

Two court cards of the same rank play the same role in different styles: a Knight of Wands charges in and acts, while a Knight of Cups pauses to weigh how a choice will feel. Read the rank for the role and the suit for how it is played.

A court card can mean a real person or an energy, and the spread position decides which: in an 'internal influences' position it is usually the querent's own traits, and in an 'external influences' position it is usually someone else or the wider environment.

No card is only good or only bad: a 'difficult' card is softened by supportive neighbours and a 'kind' card is sharpened by hard ones. Let the surrounding cards decide whether to lean into the brighter or darker side of a card's meaning.

Watch for repeating numbers and rising or falling number sequences across a spread: repeated numbers (for example, several Twos) flag a shared theme such as choice, and a rising sequence suggests something escalating while a falling one suggests it easing.

Watch which way the figures on the cards face: several figures facing left suggest a pull toward the past, several facing right a pull toward the future, two figures facing each other a conflict or meeting, and figures turned away from each other a failure to see eye to eye.

Read every card on two levels at once: the objective level, where figures stand for other people, and the subjective level, where they mirror an aspect of the querent. If it is unclear which applies, hold both readings open until the rest of the spread clarifies it.
A reversed card usually yields the opposite meaning to the same card upright.
A reading depends not only on each card's own meaning but on its place in the layout, and the cards on each side may also affect the interpretation.
Glance at the whole spread first for a preponderance of one suit: many Wands mean change, many Cups love and goodness, many Swords strife, many Pentacles political action or intrigue.
Many Major Arcana cards in a spread indicate the answer to the question is largely controlled by other people.
Make a running story out of the cards in relation to the querent rather than reading each card in isolation.

Choose a Court card as the querent's significator before shuffling, by age and coloring (Page for the young, Knight for a young man, King for a married mature man, Queen for a woman over twenty-one), or by temperament; the layout may direct it to the center of the spread or back into the deck.
Knights in a spread may mean the coming or going of a matter, and Court cards generally may stand for people or for traits rather than a person.
A card's meaning is narrowed by the House it falls in: the Two of Cups on Leo (5th House, the heart) means a love affair, while on Aquarius (11th House, friendship) it means a new friendship.
A card on the right-hand branch of the Tree is read with mercy and compassion, on the left-hand branch with severity, and on the middle branch in a spirit of harmony.
If the querent's significator card turns up in the spread, look with special attention at that position on the Tree.
If the cards do not seem to respond, have the querent shuffle again and concentrate more deeply; if they still make no sense, put them away for at least twenty-four hours before trying again.
Never finish a reading on a discouraging note: show how the querent can overcome problems by work, study, care of health, or more love and compassion in relationships.
Read the spread as a whole first — overall colors, whether the images feel dramatic or peaceful, harmony versus contrast, and your own feeling gazing at it — before interpreting any single card.
Check for preponderances and voids: many Major Arcana or mostly Minor, court cards present, aces, many cards of one suit, a suit entirely absent, or several cards sharing the same number.

Many Major Arcana cards mean forces beyond your control are at work — fate, destiny, or past actions now manifesting — and you may have little choice in the outcome; a spread of mostly Minor Arcana means the future is in your own hands.
A suit dominating a reading names the life area in question: several Cups point to a relationship, Pentacles to finances; each suit is a realm of activity and growth.
Repeated numbers carry weight: lots of Fours and Eights signal stability, Fives signal change; in a time-oriented spread, low numbers early and higher numbers later show development.

Court cards often represent real people in the querent's life, but they can also be the querent's own traits or influences in the environment — and gender is flexible, so a King can stand for a strong businesswoman; Pages are messengers, students or apprentices, youths, or immature adults.

Reversed cards are read three ways by different readers: weakened, more negative or dark, or revealing hidden, esoteric undercurrents (Mary K. Greer: the shamanic perspective and dream-time versus surface reality). Choose your approach, or read upright only.

Contradictory cards in one spread can both be true: an upright Hermit beside the Devil means seek inner guidance to resolve the Devil's restrictions; the cards also answer the most urgent matter on your mind even if you asked about something else.
A pip card's meaning comes from number plus suit, not only its picture — when the two disagree, as with the Eight of Cups, trust whichever your intuition hooks into.
A card's meaning is multiplied by its position: combine card meaning with position meaning, and treat the relationships between cards as important as the individual cards.

Yes/No system: a Major Arcana card is Yes if you are willing to do the work it asks, No if not; Minor Arcana even numbers are Yes, odd are No; King is No, Queen Yes, Knight No, Page Yes; a reversed Yes card means delay, a reversed No card means obstacles will prevent it.

Aces are gifts from the universe (Barbara Moore's phrase): a seed planted, a new opportunity offered — but you must follow through, it will not happen automatically; an Ace can also mean withdrawing into isolation to nurture a new idea before going public.
Cards that pop out of the deck while shuffling are significant: set them aside as extra commentary on the reading, or consider them and shuffle them back in.
Watch for repeated numbers: if three Twos appear in a five-card reading, a decision needs making — the other cards show what the decision is about.
Read a card with its neighbors as one story: the same event can be Death, Tower, and Devil at once, and each card adds a true facet rather than contradicting the others.

What is missing speaks: no Cups in a love reading may mean a frivolous crush or an uninterested object of affection; no Pentacles may mean love without stability; no Wands, love without chemistry; no Swords, no communication or healthy conflict; no Majors, a situation smaller than it feels; no Court cards, a lack of control or leadership.

If a Court card's meaning is unclear — you or someone else? — pull a Major Arcana clarifier: a character card means an external person, a lesson card like Judgment or the Wheel means an internal influence; the Fool is the exception and almost always means an internal influence.

To identify what kind of reversal you have, flip through the deck to the first Major Arcana card and use it as a key: it can indicate whether the reversal means opposite, loss, hidden, stalled, diminished, or 'pay attention'.
Pair a Major Arcana card with each numbered Minor card in turn and read the pair as a message — the Major sets the theme, the Minor shows how it plays out in daily life.
Notice where the figures point and look: a reversed Knight of Wands aiming his wand at the Empress can be a direct instruction, such as to call your mother.

In reversed cards, watch for 'looking-back' figures — the horse glancing at its rider in the 6 of Wands, the bird looking back in the 9 of Pentacles — they invite you to see the situation from another person's viewpoint.
Compare what you deliberately choose with what the deck randomly deals: the gap between your chosen cards and Tarot's cards is where Tarot's own voice appears, separate from your projection.

Pull clarifying cards sparingly — no more than seven extra in a reading (three for the first three, one per card, plus a final messenger) — and if seven clarifiers still do not clarify, stop, note the reading, and reflect on it later.

For a yes/no answer, count upright versus reversed in three cards: three upright is a strong yes, two upright one reversed is a qualified yes, one upright two reversed is unlikely but not impossible, three reversed is a strong no — and the cards still explain why.

If the majority of cards in a spread are reversed, consider flipping them all: pull one more card — upright means flip the spread, reversed means leave it — or read the general themes instead of each reversal; a mostly-reversed reading often means you are stuck and major changes are needed.
Numbers gain meaning from frequency and grouping: pulling all four of one number, or noticing which number completes first when sorting the deck, reveals what that number is trying to tell you.

A reversed card is not always negative and an upright card is not always good: a reversed Hanged Man can mean sudden freedom, while an upright 'good' card like the 3 of Cups can warn of overindulgence.
Do not reshuffle a scary card away: the card will manifest anyway, and re-dealing tells Tarot you do not trust its voice, which disrupts the language you have built together.

Numerology links pair major arcana cards by digit-sum (for example VII The Chariot with XVI The Tower, since 1+6=7): read the pair as a light-and-shadow story, where one card shows what the other becomes if its energy goes wrong — or what recovery looks like after it.

Compositional affinity: when two cards share the same visual layout, compare them — VI The Lovers and XV The Devil mirror each other (two figures under a presiding power), so the Devil reads as love's shadow side, choice turned to bondage.

A symbol that repeats across cards in one reading is the thread of the reading: the star in the Hermit's lamp and on XVII The Star, the sunflowers on the Queen of Wands and in the Sun's garden, the red feather on the Fool, Death and the Sun's child. Name the shared symbol and read the cards through it.

The Yod droplets link the Ace of Cups, XVI The Tower and XVIII The Moon, and the five streams link the Ace of Cups and XVII The Star — the same divine fire or flow of feeling appears in very different contexts, so ask what the shared symbol is doing in each card.

Major-minor links run through the deck: all Aces link to I The Magician (beginnings), all Knights to VII The Chariot (journeys), all Queens to III The Empress (the mother archetype), all Kings to IV The Emperor (the father archetype). A court card can be read as one face of its major.
Court-card facing direction is a timing cue: facing right looks to the future, facing left looks to the past. Use it to tell whether a person or influence is arriving or leaving.

A card or symbol that recurs across many readings means you are still in that card's energy — either you are on your path and it reassures you, or there is something to learn and the card stays until it is learned. When the situation changes, the card usually disappears.
XIX The Sun cancels out negative cards nearby — the only card Dean gives that power to. A Sun beside a difficult card softens or overrides it.

In an advice or balance position, the suit of a minor arcana card changes the advice: Wands (Fire) means push through with drive, Cups means gentle negotiation, Swords means an intellectual solution, Pentacles means do only what is practical and protect your boundaries.
In a decision spread, the suit of a minor card in a position adds a layer: Swords in an advantage position says a logical approach is best, while Cups says follow your intuition.

For cards that are already challenging, the reversed meaning can say the worst is over — the reversed Devil and the reversed Five of Cups both turn toward recovery and acceptance rather than deepening the difficulty.
Read several cards together like a storyboard: what is unfolding across the images, how are the figures interacting or not, and what story do the cards tell as a sequence?

If many Court cards appear in a reading, many other people will affect the situation — and remember you can be any Court yourself, regardless of age or gender; a Court can show which role you are playing right now.

Use the numbers as a thread: Aces are new beginnings, Twos are choices, Threes are creativity, Fours are stability, Fives are change and crossroads, Sixes are balance, Sevens are challenges, Eights are movement, Nines are near-completion, and Tens are endings and fulfilment.

If a frightening or 'bad' card appears in a position, pull up to three advice cards for it rather than leaving the querent with fear — there is no such thing as a bad card, only a hard message that needs guidance.
In a mediumship reading, read each group of three cards as a whole — the three journey cards together, then the three message cards together — rather than card by card.
When comparing options, pull one card per option and see what stands out; each position can then spawn its own clarifying pull to narrow the choice down.
A clarifying card is fine when you need more information, but pull no more than one — too many clarifiers muddle the reading.
Watch for repeated cards, suits, or numbers across a spread: patterns that keep showing up over days or weeks are the message, while one-off cards can be let go.
If two significators land next to each other in the deck during a mediumship reading, that is a sign the departed person is with the querent at the time of the reading.
Let the querent speak first about what a card says to them: ask what they feel a card reveals about their situation instead of interpreting it for them, especially in sensitive readings.

A reading is built in layers: first you see the image, then you rebuild it in your mind, then you tag it with memory and emotion, then you link it to other images through association and metaphor — and only then does a story emerge. Read cards in that order, from image to story.

Meaning comes from association, not from the card alone: each image is broken apart by the brain and reassembled with your own memories, culture, and emotional tags, so the same card legitimately means different things to different readers.

Cards link through shared associations: when two cards share a color, figure, mood, or memory tag, the brain connects them, and that connection — not either card alone — is often where the reading's real message lives.

Metaphor is the bridge between cards: the brain constantly translates images into metaphors to understand how we fit into the world, so ask what each card is a metaphor for in the querent's life, then weave the metaphors into one narrative.

A spread is a narrative arc with a beginning, middle, and end, and the listener's brain engages most when it can follow that arc. Arrange the cards as a plot — situation, tension, resolution — rather than a list of separate meanings.

Watch for overfitting: the first card can set a theme that then bends every later card to fit it. Ask whether your interpretation follows the cards or just confirms the story you formed before the first card was laid.

Expectation shapes what you see next: the brain anticipates the next card or the next turn in the story based on patterns so far, and a mismatch between expectation and what appears is information, not failure — it is the moment to recalibrate.

A prediction error is a gift: when a card contradicts what you expected, do not force it into your narrative. Pause, notice the disconnect, and let the surprise revise the story — that is how the brain learns.

The querent completes the story: the reader narrates, but the querent holds the fuller picture — their life, emotions, and hidden details — so the meaning of a card combination is only finished when the querent recognizes themselves in it.

Intuition works like a sieve: the brain takes in far more than consciousness can hold, filters out what is not needed right now, and leaves the ore — the few details that matter — from which narratives and decisions are made. Trust the filtered result, then reflect on it later.

Suit energies combine as elements of the living world: the book reimagines the suits as animal kingdoms — Cups as molluscs (mystery, desire, illusion), Pentacles as mammals (material, earthy, embodied), Swords as birds (air, movement, sharp perception), Wands as insects (fire, passion, cooperative energy) — so a spread can be read as an ecology of instincts, not just four categories.
Give the order of the cards a consistent meaning — Papez reads left to right as past, present, future — and apply it the same way every time so the sequence adds context.

Do not usually factor major arcana cards into the elemental count; instead count how many majors are present — few or none means the reading is flexible and changeable, half or more means it is more fixed.
Read connected pairs as two sides of the same coin — Fool/World, Magician/Strength, Lovers/Devil, Tower/Star — so one card explains the other's shadow and light.

To tell easily confused cards apart, compare them visually (what is similar, what is different), compare your keywords for each, and answer the same question with each card to feel how they differ in practice.

Place a card in its suit's story: the Six of Swords' escape follows the Five of Swords' tyranny, and the Eight of Cups' departure follows the Seven of Cups' fantasising — where a card falls in its suit changes its meaning.
Remember the ace is the seed of its suit and the page is the person who plants that seed — both mean beginnings, but one is potential and the other is the beginner who acts on it.
Add steps only as far as they help: keyword math first, then order, then elements and numbers, then directionality — and prune back to the simplest method if a step makes reading harder.
You do not have to show your work: as long as you reach an answer that fits, how you got there is yours alone.

When a card is reversed, try modifying it one of seven ways (Greer Step 12, Modification): read it as No/Not, as excessive or over- or undercompensating, as misused or misdirected, through 're-' words (re-do, re-think, return), as rectification (what needs correcting), as unconventional, shamanic, magical or humorous, or by reverting to the upright meaning.

In a three-card triad, elemental dignities change a card's strength (Greer Step 14, Dignity & Theme): a card between two contrary cards is little affected by either, while a card contrary to both its flankers is weakened.
Read a card as a metaphor (Greer Step 8, Metaphor): 'this card is like...' — the metaphor you reach for can unlock a meaning the keywords miss.

notes:
Where the books disagree: on reversals, Papez treats them as optional and argues the tarot is already balanced between light and shadow, while Clark calls dual upright/reversed meanings the more traditional and more nuanced method, and Esselmont offers four reversal methods (internalised energy, too much or too little, blocked, upside-down imagery) and advises picking one method for a whole reading. On the Celtic Cross tenth position, Papez reads it as the key to the outcome rather than the outcome itself, while Fiebig's Celtic/Sun Cross variations call the tenth card the outcome, goal, or task. On elements, Ethony's interaction table (fire-earth oppose, water-air oppose, air-earth merely dilute) differs from the classic Golden Dawn elemental dignities, where fire-earth and water-air are neutral rather than opposing; the app should treat Ethony's version as one system, not the only one. On numbers, Fiebig argues numbers have no inherent meaning beyond their functional value, while Esselmont and Papez both use numerology (repeating numbers, digit sums) as a live interpretive tool. On the five-card spread, Fiebig defines no single standard five-card layout — the five-card set used here (Situation / Challenge / Guidance / Hidden influence / Outcome) is the standard general-purpose layout, while Fiebig's own five-card variants include the Trend (what you have, what you are looking for, what you should do, what you want, what is important now) and Present and Future, both catalogued or noted here. Every principle in this file is grounded in a named source, and the elemental interaction rules are Ethony's system rather than a universal one. What the books do not cover: none of the sources gives a systematic table of how specific card pairs combine beyond Esselmont's per-card suggested combinations, so pair-level meanings must be computed from the keyword-addition and elemental rules rather than looked up; none gives rules for chains of three or more cards beyond Papez's five-step method; none addresses how a user's personal lexicon should override or blend with a traditional combination reading; none gives rules for reversed cards in specific spread positions beyond the general reversal methods; and none covers timing in combinations except Ethony's court-card timing chapter, which is not summarised here. The Fiebig book contains 122 layouts; this catalog is a curated 11, chosen for general-purpose use, and the app's 1-, 3-, and 5-card spreads are listed first.

Eden Gray adds three full spreads (Ancient Celtic Method, Horoscope Method, Tree of Life Method), each with a complete sample reading, plus suit-preponderance and significator rules. She gives no dedicated two-card pair-combination chapter and no short 1- or 3-card spreads. Her Ancient Celtic Method is a distinct variant from the Celtic Cross already in the catalog (Papez's position set) — both are kept. Her Tree of Life chapter also describes a full Life-reading variant (seven cards at each Tree position, spread three times for past/present/future, at most once a year per querent). On clarifiers, Weber allows up to seven clarifying cards for a question, while Reed advises drawing at most one — the two books disagree on how many clarifiers a reading should use. Greer (21 Ways) is partial coverage: the book is a scanned image-only PDF with no text layer, so only a bounded sample of 20 pages was read — the contents (all 21 steps) plus Steps 8 (Metaphor), 12 (Modification) and 14 (Dignity & Theme) in detail; the full text was not extracted.

positional_rules.rule: A spread position is half the interpretation: combine the card's meaning with the position's meaning to get the reading. The same card means something different in every slot it lands in.
A card in a past position shows roots and influences — what shaped the present — not a prediction. Read it as background that is still active, not as something finished and gone.
A card in a present position shows the live energy of the situation right now: what is happening, what is on the querent's mind, and what they can act on today.

A card in a future position shows direction and tendency, not a fixed fate. It describes where things are headed if nothing changes, and it can be renamed as a tendency or next step for readers who do not read predictively.

A card laid across another (the crossing card) modifies it for good or bad: it either supports the card beneath it or blocks and challenges it. Read the pair together, not the crossing card on its own.

A card in a challenge or obstacle position is read as a block even if it is a normally 'positive' card: ask what about this energy is getting in the way, being overdone, or arriving at the wrong time.
A card in a strength, talent, or chance position is read as a resource even if it is a normally 'difficult' card: ask what this energy offers, what it makes possible, and how it can be used well.
A card in a hidden or unconscious position shows what the querent does not yet see: influences, motives, or facts operating below awareness. Read it as context the querent needs, not as a verdict.
A card in an advice or guidance position is counsel, not description: it says what to do or how to approach the situation, rather than what is happening.
A card in an outcome position is best read as the key to the outcome — what the querent needs to do to reach the best result — rather than a fixed prediction of what will happen.

Read paired positions as a dialogue: past with future, conscious with unconscious, internal with external. Each pair shows the same situation from two angles, and the contrast between them is often the most useful part of the reading.

A reversed card in a position can mean the energy is internalised or private, too much or too little, or blocked — pick one method for the whole reading before you begin, then let the position narrow it: a reversed card in an obstacle slot usually means blocked, in a hopes slot usually means an inner fear.
A card in a root or foundation position grounds the whole reading: it names what the question grew out of. If the outcome is unclear, re-read the root — the answer usually traces back to it.
Position 2 (This Crosses Him) is laid across position 1 and is always read as if it were right side up, even when it falls reversed.
Each of the twelve Houses governs a department of life, and the card falling there must be blended with that House's meaning to fit the pair.
The Daath Pack of seven cards, set aside during the layout, is turned up and read only after the rest of the reading is completed, from right to left, to qualify and enlarge upon the ten Tree cards.

If the final outcome card yields no clear conclusion, the whole operation may be repeated with the tenth card taking the place of the querent's significator card, for a more detailed account of the outcome.

In timeline spreads, compare the beginning and the end: negative cards in the past and positive ones in the future show progress and better days ahead; the reverse suggests you are not handling the situation well, or things may get worse before they get better.

Notice where Major Arcana cards fall: early or in the past portion means forces already set in motion; toward the end or future means destiny unfolding ahead; a trump in an opportunity position versus an obstacle position changes its weight — always pay a trump extra attention wherever it lands.

In spreads describing levels of awareness, such as the World Tree, check whether the levels are harmonious or incongruous — calm images in one section and disturbing ones in another, or a coordinated flow.

In spreads describing different life areas, such as the Horoscope or Feng Shui spreads, check whether positive cards cluster in some areas while negative ones appear in others, and whether cards fall into positions that fit or conflict with their basic natures.
If a Significator is left in the deck and turns up in the spread, the position it occupies becomes particularly important.
An outcome or future position shows what is likely if things continue as they are — change your actions, thoughts, or feelings and the outcome can change, so update a reading every few months.

Near future and distant future are relative: near may mean days for one person and weeks for another, distant weeks to months; the cards show what is likely but are poor at fixed time limits, so allow leeway.
In the Goal Seeking spread, the two cards surrounding your deliberately chosen outcome card show what flanks and influences that outcome.

In the How Long spread, the cards lying between the Fool (the beginning) and the World (the outcome) mark the events between now and the goal, each card standing for one unit of time — days, weeks, months, or years, whichever is reasonable.
In a Couple's Reading, each partner gets a column and the horizontal cards are shared experiences; a majority pointing one way means one person is giving or taking too much.
In the Monthly Forecast, the three cards for each week read left to right as blessing, challenge, and general theme.

In the Seasonal Forecast, each season's triangle reads bottom-left blessing, bottom-right challenge, top unexpected, with a crowning card as the soul's lesson for the season — and a seventeenth center card as the year's lesson.
In the Follow the Wand spread, the cards surrounding the Ace of Wands show how to develop a passion — what feeds it and what blocks it.
In the Roles We Play spread, four Majors read as the largest role you play to others, the smallest role, how you challenge others, and how you bless others.
In a Journey in a Day reading, five Majors laid left to right are morning, midday, early afternoon, late afternoon, and evening — the same archetypes at the scale of one ordinary day.
In the Present Triangle, the positions include the past, the present, the future, the effects of the past on the present, and the root cause of the situation.
In the Storyboard reading, three cards read as beginning, middle, and end of a single story, like panels of a comic strip.
Where a character in a card is looking or pointing can act as a position in itself, directing the card's message toward another card or a real-world action.
An overseeing or significator card sets the theme of the reading and is read first in spirit and last in turn: the drawn cards answer inside the frame it provides, not independently of it.
The bottom card of the deck can be used as a hidden-truth position: it reveals what is concealed beneath the visible spread.

In the Ten spread, position order tells an endings-to-beginnings story: what is ending, what to do now, what supports you, a secret, then what is coming next — a card in the 'ending' position is closing, the same card in the 'coming next' position is opening.

In the portal spread the layout is a journey: the present sits below the High Priestess and the future above her, so the reading moves upward through the gateway from what you are learning now to how that wisdom will shape your life.

Reversed cards in any position are optional to read as reversed: the shadow side of a card is always present in its upright meaning, so you may turn a reversed card upright and read its shadow from the upright instead — except the Sun, which chases all shadows away.
In the Body Mind Spirit spread, the same card reads as physical state, mental state, or spiritual state depending on its position — a card that is solid in Mind can still flag burnout in Body.

In the Chakra spread, position is the energy centre: Root is survival and security, Sacral is creativity and pleasure, Solar Plexus is willpower, Heart is love and connection, Throat is communication, Third Eye is intuition, Crown is awareness.
In the Grief spread, the five positions follow the stages of grief — what to look at now, what anger teaches, finding peace in the present, what sadness is saying, and what must be accepted.

In the Mediumship spread, the first three cards after the significators describe the soul's journey and the last three carry the spirit's messages — the same card reads as journey or message depending on which group it falls in.
In the Guardian Angel spread, cards are read in three groups of three: what you need to know about your angel, how to connect, and what messages they have for you now.

In the Situation, What You Need to Know, and Advice spread, the middle card exists to illuminate what you are missing or ignoring — the hidden or overlooked aspect — while the last card is guidance, not prediction.
A card drawn for the day answers only that day's question — what is most meaningful today, or how to make the most of today — and should not be stretched into a long-term forecast.
Position turns an image into a role: the same card means something different as the self, the problem, a past bias, or a future plan, because each position asks a different question of the image.
A past position is about memory and bias: it shows how long-term memories and learned inhibitions are steering the present, not just what happened before.
A future position is about expectation and planning: it reveals what the querent anticipates and is already rehearsing, so it can show a plan — or a self-fulfilling expectation worth questioning.
A position that represents the other person asks for empathy, not projection: read it by imagining their feelings and motives, not by importing your own state.

In a narrative-arc layout, the middle position holds the roadblock: the card there is not the obstacle in the world but the querent's resistance to hearing or accepting the story, which is often the most useful card in the spread.
The final position is action, not fate: it shows what happens when thought becomes movement in the world — the outcome of the choices made, not a fixed destiny.
An anticipation position works by staying closed: keeping a card face-down while you write down what you expect it to be exposes your biases before the image can confirm them.

In the Celtic Cross, position 7 (internal influences) is what is within the querent's control — a court card there shows the querent's own traits — while position 8 (external influences) is outside their control, and a court card there usually means someone else.
In the Celtic Cross, position 9 holds the greatest hope AND the greatest fear together — the two are usually the same thing, or two sides of the same coin.

A single card becomes a spread when you give its position a name or focus — daily advice, evening reflection, preparation, or a focus for the day — which gives the card context to work with.

spreads.purpose: Read three cards as a single story — beginning, middle, and end — like panels of a comic strip, answering 'What is my current story?'

positions.label: Beginning
positions.meaning: How the story starts.

positions.label: Middle
positions.meaning: How the story develops.

positions.label: End
positions.meaning: How the story resolves.

spreads.name: Star of Guidance
spreads.purpose: An eight-pointed-star layout using the seven classical planets to reveal talents, challenges and potential; a significator is laid first and turned last.

positions.label: Significator
positions.meaning: The theme of the reading

positions.label: You and your situation
positions.meaning: Where you stand now

positions.label: Mercury: immediate influences
positions.meaning: What is flowing in your life

positions.label: Mars: challenges
positions.meaning: Conflict and power struggles

positions.label: Venus: relationships
positions.meaning: Love and partnerships

positions.label: Saturn: lessons
positions.meaning: What you are learning, or what lesson is repeating

positions.label: Jupiter: skills and experience
positions.meaning: How you shine in the world

positions.label: Moon: what is hidden
positions.meaning: Unconscious beliefs and what is hidden from you

positions.label: The Sun: the outcome
positions.meaning: Your greatest potential at this time

spreads.name: The Ten: Endings and Beginnings
spreads.purpose: Built on the Roman numeral X, the number of endings that make way for beginnings; reveals what will be released and what is to come.

positions.label: What's coming to an end
positions.meaning: What is closing in this situation

positions.label: What's before you
positions.meaning: What to do now

positions.label: What supports you financially
positions.meaning: Material backing for the change

positions.label: What supports you emotionally
positions.meaning: Emotional backing for the change

positions.label: A secret about this situation
positions.meaning: What is hidden or unspoken

positions.label: What's coming next
positions.meaning: What arrives after the ending

spreads.name: Fortune's Wheel: Cycles of Change
spreads.purpose: Built around X The Wheel of Fortune; explores cycles of growth, fulfilment, release and gratitude, optionally with a second wheel layered on top and a pendulum to find your place in the cycle.

positions.label: What to appreciate
positions.meaning: What deserves gratitude now

positions.label: What to reflect on
positions.meaning: What to sit with and consider

positions.label: What to release
positions.meaning: What to let go of

positions.label: What's over
positions.meaning: What has already ended

positions.label: Underlying support
positions.meaning: What holds you up

positions.label: What I need to share
positions.meaning: What to give or express

positions.label: What's getting stronger
positions.meaning: What is growing

positions.label: Blessings
positions.meaning: What is gifted to you

spreads.name: Authority, Boundaries, Illumination (Justice)
spreads.purpose: Dean's example of designing your own spread: take three symbol meanings from one card and turn each into a position.

positions.label: Authority
positions.meaning: What am I in charge of, or responsible for?

positions.label: Boundaries
positions.meaning: What do I need to protect?

positions.label: Illumination
positions.meaning: What do I need to see now?

spreads.name: The Birthday Reading (The Fool)
spreads.purpose: A year-ahead reading overseen by the Fool, the newborn beginner of the major arcana cycle.

positions.label: What you have learned
positions.meaning: What you have learned from the past twelve months

positions.label: What is seeking you now
positions.meaning: What is arriving or calling to you

positions.label: Spiritual guidance
positions.meaning: Spiritual guidance for the year ahead

spreads.name: Making Magic (The Magician)
spreads.purpose: Discover your potential to create what you desire, overseen by the Magician.

positions.label: What you can create
positions.meaning: What you are able to bring into being

positions.label: Resources needed
positions.meaning: What kind of resources you need

positions.label: The magic ingredient
positions.meaning: What turns your idea into gold

spreads.name: The Other Side of the Portal (The High Priestess)
spreads.purpose: Travel through the Priestess's gateway from present to future, with her card placed in the centre.

positions.label: The present
positions.meaning: What I am learning now

positions.label: The future
positions.meaning: How this wisdom will affect my life

spreads.name: Money and Abundance (The Empress)
spreads.purpose: Tune in to the creative energy of number III to check for blocks in abundance.

positions.label: What's in the way
positions.meaning: What blocks abundance

positions.label: What to do
positions.meaning: What to focus on to grow in abundance

spreads.name: Being the Emperor (The Emperor)
spreads.purpose: Uses the Emperor's organizing skills to reveal what you most need to manage at present.

positions.label: Past success
positions.meaning: A success to stand on

positions.label: Your situation
positions.meaning: What to take charge of now

positions.label: Guidance
positions.meaning: Moving on from the situation in card 2

spreads.name: Lessons and Blessings (The Hierophant)
spreads.purpose: Acknowledge and appreciate what you are learning; gratitude opens the way to further lessons.

positions.label: The situation now
positions.meaning: Where things stand

positions.label: Your current lesson
positions.meaning: What you are learning about yourself through this situation

positions.label: Blessings
positions.meaning: What you can be grateful for; skills and challenges that help with the lesson

spreads.name: You and Them (The Lovers)
spreads.purpose: A fast look at what each person brings to a relationship, new or established.

positions.label: What you bring
positions.meaning: The qualities you bring to the relationship

positions.label: What they bring
positions.meaning: The qualities the other person brings

positions.label: The outcome
positions.meaning: Where the relationship is heading

spreads.name: Where Am I Going? (The Chariot)
spreads.purpose: The Chariot's progress as a small spread for what can move forward next in your life.

positions.label: Where you are now
positions.meaning: Your current position

positions.label: Where you are going
positions.meaning: The direction of travel

positions.label: What to do next
positions.meaning: The next step to take

spreads.name: Finding Resilience (Strength)
spreads.purpose: Draw on energy reserves to stay strong and focused when you need to.

positions.label: How to recharge
positions.meaning: How best to recharge your energy: what to avoid or do more of

positions.label: Resources and support
positions.meaning: Resources and support available

positions.label: Likely outcome
positions.meaning: Where this leads

spreads.name: Healing Within (The Hermit)
spreads.purpose: Look at healing and what you may need to soothe in yourself.

positions.label: How you are feeling
positions.meaning: How you are feeling this moment

positions.label: What needs care
positions.meaning: What aspect of your life needs care and attention

positions.label: The benefit
positions.meaning: How this approach can benefit you going forward

spreads.name: Ups and Downs (The Wheel of Fortune)
spreads.purpose: A simple spread taking its inspiration from the Wheel's cycles of fortune.

positions.label: The upside
positions.meaning: The upside of your present situation

positions.label: The downside
positions.meaning: The downside of your situation

positions.label: The outcome
positions.meaning: Where the cycle is heading

spreads.name: Make That Decision (Justice)
spreads.purpose: A three-card decision spread overseen by Justice; note the suits of any minor cards as well as their meanings.

positions.label: Strengths
positions.meaning: What favours this choice

positions.label: Weaknesses
positions.meaning: What counts against it

positions.label: Advice
positions.meaning: What to do

spreads.name: Trust Issues (The Hanged Man)
spreads.purpose: Built on the Hanged Man's thin tether: what or whom you can trust, the doubt, and advice.

positions.label: What you trust
positions.meaning: What or whom you trust or believe in

positions.label: Doubt
positions.meaning: What to commit to or walk away from

positions.label: Advice
positions.meaning: Advice going forward

spreads.name: What's on the Horizon? (Death)
spreads.purpose: Looks at what may be ending, how best to manage it, and what comes next.

positions.label: What is to be transformed
positions.meaning: What is ending or changing

positions.label: What you need
positions.meaning: What you need to move forward

positions.label: What's on the horizon
positions.meaning: What comes next

spreads.name: Balancing Opposites (Temperance)
spreads.purpose: Find a way forward when dealing with opposing demands; Temperance herself is position 1.

positions.label: The situation now
positions.meaning: Where things stand (Temperance oversees)

positions.label: Negative impact
positions.meaning: The negative impact of your situation or relationship

positions.label: Positive potential
positions.meaning: The positive potential of your situation or relationship

positions.label: Guidance
positions.meaning: Where to find balance

spreads.name: Hidden Truth (The Devil)
spreads.purpose: Find the hidden truth that unlocks a stuck situation, using the bottom card of the deck as the final position.

positions.label: The reason
positions.meaning: The reason for this situation

positions.label: What needs to change
positions.meaning: What has to shift

positions.label: Hidden truth
positions.meaning: The hidden truth, taken from the bottom of the deck, to help you move forward

spreads.name: Surrender and Reflection (The Tower)
spreads.purpose: The Tower is about acceptance rather than action: two face-up cards plus two new ones.

positions.label: The Tower: destruction
positions.meaning: What is breaking down

positions.label: What to surrender to
positions.meaning: What to let go of after the impact

positions.label: What to reflect on
positions.meaning: What to contemplate, including what is in and out of balance

positions.label: The Chariot: moving on
positions.meaning: How you move forward

spreads.name: Star Power (The Star)
spreads.purpose: When you have a wish: check your focus and pull in a little starlight.

positions.label: What you're creating
positions.meaning: What you are creating or manifesting now

positions.label: What to release
positions.meaning: What to release to allow your wish to manifest

positions.label: Star power
positions.meaning: Cosmic guidance

spreads.name: Moon Wisdom (The Moon)
spreads.purpose: Uses the ocean's tides to see the benefits and the challenges in any situation.

positions.label: High tide: benefits
positions.meaning: The benefits of the situation

positions.label: Low tide: challenges
positions.meaning: The challenges of the situation

positions.label: Gift or lesson
positions.meaning: The gift or lesson in it

spreads.name: Sun Light (The Sun)
spreads.purpose: When you need time to recharge and grow creatively, let these cards illuminate the way.

positions.label: What can't grow
positions.meaning: What is blocked or withering

positions.label: What should I sow
positions.meaning: What to plant or begin

positions.label: What will manifest
positions.meaning: What will grow as a result

spreads.name: Recurring Situations (The World)
spreads.purpose: The World marks completion and a new cycle; this spread reveals a recurring situation and the lesson it brings.

positions.label: The recurring situation
positions.meaning: The pattern that keeps returning

positions.label: Advice
positions.meaning: What to do about it

positions.label: Guidance for healing
positions.meaning: Guidance for healing this cycle

spreads.name: Daily Pull
spreads.purpose: Centre yourself, set an intentional day, and learn the cards through a single daily draw.

positions.label: Card for the Day
positions.meaning: What the day holds or what to focus on; journal whatever comes to mind without overthinking.

spreads.name: Body Mind Spirit Spread
spreads.purpose: Check in on your overall physical, mental, and spiritual energy, especially during illness or heavy responsibility.

positions.label: Body
positions.meaning: Your physical state and what your body needs.

positions.label: Mind
positions.meaning: Your mental state, focus, and worries.

positions.label: Spirit
positions.meaning: Your spiritual state and what restores you.

spreads.name: Chakra Spread
spreads.purpose: See whether any energy centre is blocked or out of balance; for exploration, not diagnosis.

positions.label: Root Chakra
positions.meaning: Basic needs, survival, and identity.

positions.label: Sacral Chakra
positions.meaning: Creativity, pleasure, and desire.

positions.label: Solar Plexus Chakra
positions.meaning: Willpower, self-esteem, and autonomy.

positions.label: Heart Chakra
positions.meaning: Love, compassion, and connection with others.

positions.label: Throat Chakra
positions.meaning: Communication, self-expression, and truth.

positions.label: Third Eye Chakra
positions.meaning: Intuition, imagination, and the big picture.

positions.label: Crown Chakra
positions.meaning: Awareness, knowledge, and wisdom.

spreads.name: Recovery Spread
spreads.purpose: Untangle fearful thinking while recovering from surgery, illness, or addiction.

positions.label: Present Moment
positions.meaning: Where you are right now in your recovery.

positions.label: What Do I Need Right Now?
positions.meaning: What you need in this moment.

positions.label: How Can I Continue to Support My Healing?
positions.meaning: How to keep supporting your healing going forward.

spreads.name: Boundaries Spread
spreads.purpose: Shore up boundaries with a specific person or in general, especially for caregivers.

positions.label: What Do I Need to Know About My Boundaries?
positions.meaning: What to know about your boundaries with this person right now.

positions.label: What Is Preventing Me from Setting Good Boundaries?
positions.meaning: The block that keeps you from setting limits.

positions.label: How Can I Care for My Needs in a Healthy, Happy Way?
positions.meaning: How to meet your own needs well.

positions.label: What Boundaries Can I Set Right Now to Empower Me?
positions.meaning: A boundary you can set immediately.

spreads.name: What Do I Need? Spread
spreads.purpose: Compare options for support by pulling one card per option, such as a helper, a day off, or a massage.

positions.label: Option 1
positions.meaning: What the first option would bring.

positions.label: Option 2
positions.meaning: What the second option would bring.

positions.label: Option 3
positions.meaning: What the third option would bring.

spreads.name: Three Things, Right Now Spread
spreads.purpose: Create ease when overwhelmed by finding three small changes instead of a complete overhaul.

positions.label: What Is One Thing I Can Take Off My Plate Right Now?
positions.meaning: One thing to release or delegate now.

positions.label: What Is One Habit I Can Change Right Now?
positions.meaning: One habit to change now.

positions.label: What Is One Kind Thing I Can Do for Myself Right Now?
positions.meaning: One kind thing to do for yourself now.

spreads.name: The Situation, What You Need to Know, and Advice Spread
spreads.purpose: A go-to all-purpose spread for moving through a problem with grace.

positions.label: The Situation
positions.meaning: Where you stand at the moment.

positions.label: What You Need to Know
positions.meaning: What you may be missing or ignoring.

positions.label: Advice
positions.meaning: Guidance for moving through the issue wisely.

spreads.name: Grief Spread
spreads.purpose: Work through loss using the five stages of grief; for yourself or someone grieving.

positions.label: What Do I Need to Look at Right Now?
positions.meaning: What needs attention in this moment.

positions.label: What Can I Learn from My Anger?
positions.meaning: What anger is teaching you.

positions.label: What Can I Do to Find Peace with the Present Moment?
positions.meaning: How to find peace right now.

positions.label: What Is My Sadness Trying to Tell Me?
positions.meaning: The message inside your sadness.

positions.label: What Do I Need to Accept at This Time?
positions.meaning: What acceptance is asking of you now.

spreads.name: Mediumship Spread
spreads.purpose: Learn how a departed loved one is doing on the other side and hear any messages they have.

positions.label: Querent Significator
positions.meaning: A Court card chosen for the querent, by astrological sign or identity.

positions.label: Deceased Significator
positions.meaning: A Court card chosen for the departed person; use the High Priestess if the sign is unknown, both share one significator, or it is a pet.

positions.label: The Soul's Journey — card 1
positions.meaning: Three cards read as a whole describing the departed person's journey.

positions.label: The Soul's Journey — card 2
positions.meaning: Three cards read as a whole describing the departed person's journey.

positions.label: The Soul's Journey — card 3
positions.meaning: Three cards read as a whole describing the departed person's journey.

positions.label: Messages from the Spirit — card 1
positions.meaning: Three cards read as a whole carrying the spirit's messages for the querent.

positions.label: Messages from the Spirit — card 2
positions.meaning: Three cards read as a whole carrying the spirit's messages for the querent.

positions.label: Messages from the Spirit — card 3
positions.meaning: Three cards read as a whole carrying the spirit's messages for the querent.

spreads.name: Card for the Day Spread
spreads.purpose: Stay in the present moment when facing a terminal illness, instead of looking far ahead.

positions.label: Today
positions.meaning: The most meaningful thing to do today, how to make the most of today, or what magic to expect today.

spreads.name: Meeting My Guardian Angel Spread
spreads.purpose: Connect with your guardian angel for comfort and guidance.

positions.label: What Do I Need to Know About My Guardian Angel? — card 1
positions.meaning: Three cards describing your guardian angel.

positions.label: What Do I Need to Know About My Guardian Angel? — card 2
positions.meaning: Three cards describing your guardian angel.

positions.label: What Do I Need to Know About My Guardian Angel? — card 3
positions.meaning: Three cards describing your guardian angel.

positions.label: How Can I Connect with My Guardian Angel? — card 1
positions.meaning: Three cards on how to connect with them.

positions.label: How Can I Connect with My Guardian Angel? — card 2
positions.meaning: Three cards on how to connect with them.

positions.label: How Can I Connect with My Guardian Angel? — card 3
positions.meaning: Three cards on how to connect with them.

positions.label: What Messages Does My Guardian Angel Have for Me Right Now? — card 1
positions.meaning: Three cards carrying their messages for you now.

positions.label: What Messages Does My Guardian Angel Have for Me Right Now? — card 2
positions.meaning: Three cards carrying their messages for you now.

positions.label: What Messages Does My Guardian Angel Have for Me Right Now? — card 3
positions.meaning: Three cards carrying their messages for you now.

spreads.name: The Three R's Spread
spreads.purpose: Heal after pregnancy loss or the loss of a child.

positions.label: Release: What Do I Need to Release?
positions.meaning: What to let go of.

positions.label: Recover: How Can I Recover?
positions.meaning: How to recover.

positions.label: Remember: How Do I Honor the Memory of This Child?
positions.meaning: How to honour the child's memory.

spreads.name: Past, Present, and Future Spread
spreads.purpose: A classic spread that works well after a job loss, when the focus is fixed on finding new work.

positions.label: Past
positions.meaning: What led here.

positions.label: Present
positions.meaning: Where you are now.

positions.label: Future
positions.meaning: What is coming next.

spreads.name: Now, Soon, Obstacles, The New Beginning Spread
spreads.purpose: Navigate any life change, such as the empty nest, by mapping now, soon, obstacles, and the new beginning.

positions.label: Now
positions.meaning: Where things are now.

positions.label: Soon
positions.meaning: What is coming soon.

positions.label: Obstacles
positions.meaning: What stands in the way.

positions.label: The New Beginning Looks Like...
positions.meaning: What the new beginning will look like.

spreads.name: Reflection on Aging Spread
spreads.purpose: Make peace with getting older and focus on how you feel rather than how you look.

positions.label: What Do You Need to Face About Getting Older?
positions.meaning: What aging asks you to face.

positions.label: What Is Your Inner Dialogue at This Time?
positions.meaning: What you are telling yourself about aging.

positions.label: What Can You Appreciate About Yourself Right Now?
positions.meaning: What to appreciate about yourself now.

positions.label: What Are Some Actions You Can Take to Accept Yourself Right Now?
positions.meaning: Actions that help you accept yourself.

spreads.name: The Five Remembrances Spread
spreads.purpose: Remember that life is precious and finite, based on the Buddhist Five Remembrances, and loosen grasping.

positions.label: What Do I Need to Know About Aging?
positions.meaning: What aging has to teach you.

positions.label: What Do I Need to Know About Health?
positions.meaning: What health has to teach you.

positions.label: What Do I Need to Know About Dying?
positions.meaning: What dying has to teach you.

positions.label: What Do I Need to Know About Loss?
positions.meaning: What loss has to teach you.

positions.label: What Do I Need to Know About My Karma?
positions.meaning: What your deeds and karma have to teach you.

spreads.name: Self and the Other
spreads.purpose: Overlaid on a regular spread to clarify how the reader relates to the querent — empathy, mirroring, and understanding their actions.

positions.label: Your Inner Self
positions.meaning: Where you, the reader, are emotionally at this point in the reading.

positions.label: Empathy for the Other
positions.meaning: How you perceive the other person and recognize their emotions.

positions.label: Mirroring the Other in You
positions.meaning: How you would feel in their shoes — feeling what they feel.

positions.label: Understanding the Other's Actions
positions.meaning: Their desires, influences, and choices — contemplating why they act as they do.

positions.label: Future Prognostications
positions.meaning: What they can do to resolve the situation, and the ramifications of those next steps.

spreads.name: Narrative Arc
spreads.purpose: For a querent stuck on a preconceived outcome or looping on choices — walks through plot formation, resistance, and future possibility.

positions.label: Plot Narrative
positions.meaning: The story forming in the reading — the plot as it stands.

positions.label: Roadblocks to Acceptance
positions.meaning: Why the querent may not be ready to hear the story, or finds it discordant with their expectations; ask the querent to interpret this card themselves.

positions.label: Future Contemplation
positions.meaning: The querent's crossroads — how things could unfold with different choices.

spreads.name: Anticipation Spread
spreads.purpose: Overcomes the bias of expectation and opens the reader to newer inputs; can also be used to set intentions.

positions.label: First Card
positions.meaning: Opened first; write down what you expect the second card to be before opening it.

positions.label: Second Card
positions.meaning: Opened next; notice how you feel when you see it — does it match what you expected? Ask the querent the same.

positions.label: Third Card
positions.meaning: Predict it before opening, note your feelings beforehand, then compare expectation with reality.

spreads.name: One-Card Reflection Spread
spreads.purpose: Look back at the day and reflect on its key lesson or message.

positions.label: Key lesson or message of the day
positions.meaning: What the day was trying to teach you.

spreads.name: Two-Card Personal Growth Check-In Spread
spreads.purpose: A present-time check-in on your personal growth.

positions.label: What should I be working on?
positions.meaning: The growth edge right now.

positions.label: What can help me do better?
positions.meaning: The support or approach that helps.

spreads.name: Three-Card Week- or Month-Ahead Spread
spreads.purpose: A simple forecast of what is coming up in the week or month ahead.

positions.label: Primary theme of the upcoming week/month
positions.meaning: The main thread of the period ahead.

positions.label: What to avoid this week/month
positions.meaning: What to steer clear of.

positions.label: What to embrace this week/month
positions.meaning: What to lean into.

spreads.name: Four-Card Guidance Spread
spreads.purpose: Process something weighing on your mind and find your next best steps.

positions.label: What lies at the heart of the issue?
positions.meaning: The core of the situation.

positions.label: Internal influences
positions.meaning: What is coming from inside you.

positions.label: External influences
positions.meaning: What is coming from outside you.

positions.label: Key to a favourable outcome
positions.meaning: What unlocks the best resolution.

spreads.name: One-Card Focus Spread
spreads.purpose: Drawn at the start of the day: something to keep in mind or focus on.

positions.label: Focus for the day
positions.meaning: What to hold in mind through the day ahead.

spreads.name: Two-Card Situation/Advice Spread
spreads.purpose: Quick insight for navigating a situation, good or bad.

positions.label: What do I need to know about this situation?
positions.meaning: Context and information about what is happening.

positions.label: What action should I take?
positions.meaning: Advice for the next step.

spreads.name: Three-Card Wants vs. Needs Spread
spreads.purpose: Separate what you want from what you need and bridge the gap between them.

positions.label: What you want
positions.meaning: The desire pulling at you.

positions.label: What you need
positions.meaning: What would actually serve you.

positions.label: How to bridge the gap
positions.meaning: How to move from want toward need.

spreads.name: Four-Card Life Learning Spread
spreads.purpose: Draw lessons from past and present and integrate them into what comes next.

positions.label: Something you can learn from your past
positions.meaning: A past lesson still relevant.

positions.label: Something you can learn from your present
positions.meaning: What the present is teaching.

positions.label: What you need to learn next
positions.meaning: Where to focus your learning.

positions.label: How to integrate this knowledge
positions.meaning: How to put the lessons together.

spreads.name: One-Card Embodiment Spread
spreads.purpose: Pull a court card for qualities to embody in the day or week ahead.

positions.label: Qualities to embody
positions.meaning: Lean into this character's strengths and work past their struggles.

spreads.name: Two-Card Situation/Advice Spread (Court Cards)
spreads.purpose: Explore a predicament through court-card personalities and energies.

positions.label: What do I need to know about this situation?
positions.meaning: Use the court card to understand the energy or personality of the situation.

positions.label: What action should I take?
positions.meaning: Use the court card to find the best approach to navigate it.

spreads.name: Three-Card Me, Them, Us Spread
spreads.purpose: A relationship spread for any kind of relationship — romantic, platonic, professional, or familial.

positions.label: Me
positions.meaning: Personality traits coming forward prominently for you.

positions.label: Them
positions.meaning: Personality traits coming forward prominently for the other person.

positions.label: Us
positions.meaning: Traits both should lean into to create more harmony.

spreads.name: Four-Card Personal Development Spread
spreads.purpose: Explore your own personal growth and development.

positions.label: Strengths to lean into
positions.meaning: What is already working for you.

positions.label: Struggles you are currently dealing with
positions.meaning: What is getting in the way.

positions.label: Advice from a court card
positions.meaning: What advice would this character give you about your struggles?

positions.label: Action step to take
positions.meaning: What would this court card do next?

spreads.name: Daily Advice
spreads.purpose: One card taken as advice for a better day today.

positions.label: Advice for today
positions.meaning: Start with a single-sentence piece of advice, then journal deeper if you like.

spreads.name: Evening Reflection
spreads.purpose: Look back on the day at its end and learn from what happened.

positions.label: What lesson can I learn from my experiences today?
positions.meaning: Frame the interpretation as a question to sit with.

spreads.name: Preparation
spreads.purpose: A daily forecast that empowers you to be prepared for the day ahead.

positions.label: What do I need to be prepared for today?
positions.meaning: Read literally or metaphorically — what is coming, and how to meet it.

spreads.name: Within, Without, Advice
spreads.purpose: Untangle a situation into inner influences, outer forces, and what to do.

positions.label: Within
positions.meaning: Internal influences — thoughts or emotions about the subject.

positions.label: Without
positions.meaning: External forces outside your control.

positions.label: Advice
positions.meaning: What to consider or how to act.

spreads.name: Energy, Obstacle, Advice
spreads.purpose: Papez's own favourite three-card spread, created because the popular ones left her wanting more.

positions.label: Energy
positions.meaning: What is going on energetically with the situation.

positions.label: Obstacle
positions.meaning: What is causing trouble.

positions.label: Advice
positions.meaning: How to move forward.
